Beeswarm plot for neighbourhood-level metrics

Source: R/plot_nhood_beeswarm.R
plot_nhood_beeswarm.Rd

Accepts a data frame with neighbourhoods as rows.

Usage

plot_nhood_beeswarm(
  nhood_data,
  plot_cols,
  reliability_col = NULL,
  group_by,
  summary_metric = c("global_mean", "none", "global_median", "group_mean",
    "group_median"),
  colour_by = NULL,
  p_val_col = "p_val",
  LFC_col = "LFC",
  sig_threshold = 0.1,
  size_by = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  alpha = 0.8,
  facet_by = NULL,
  facet_ncol = NULL,
  facet_scales = c("free", "fixed", "free_x", "free_y"),
  x_limits = NULL,
  x_lab = NULL,
  y_lab = NULL,
  title = "",
  subtitle = NULL
)

Arguments

nhood_data

Data frame containing all columns to plot.

plot_cols

Character vector of column name(s) to use as the x-axis. Supply one name for a single-metric plot, or multiple names to get one panel row per metric (multi-column mode).

reliability_col

Column name of a logical reliability flag. Rows where this column is FALSE or NA are dropped before plotting. NULL skips reliability filtering entirely.

group_by

Column name (string) whose levels form the y-axis categories.

summary_metric

Controls whether a summary line is drawn, which statistic is used, and whether it is computed globally or per group. One of:

  • "none" – no summary line is drawn.

  • "global_mean" – (default) one dashed vertical line per panel at the grand mean across all group_by levels.

  • "global_median" – as above but using the median.

  • "group_mean" – one short vertical segment per group_by level at the per-group mean. Segments span ±0.4 y-units so they sit within each beeswarm row.

  • "group_median" – as above but using the median.

colour_by

Column name (string) for point colour. NULL defaults to group_by. Set to the value of LFC_col to activate p-value-filtered LFC colouring.

p_val_col

Column name of p-values (used in LFC mode).

LFC_col

Column name of log-fold-changes (used in LFC mode).

sig_threshold

Significance threshold; points with p < sig_threshold are coloured by LFC in LFC mode.

size_by

Column name (string) to map point size to, or NULL (default) for a fixed point size.

size

Controls point size and depends on size_by:

  • When size_by is NULL — a single numeric giving the fixed point size (default 2 when size is left NULL).

  • When size_by is a column name — a numeric vector of length 2 giving the minimum and maximum point size of the size scale (default c(1, 4) when size is left NULL).

alpha

Numeric between 0-1. Point transparency (default 0.8).

facet_by

Column name to facet by, or NULL. In multi-column mode this produces a facet_grid (metric rows x facet_by cols); in single-column mode it produces a facet_wrap.

facet_ncol

Number of columns for facet_wrap (NULL = auto). Ignored when facet_grid is used.

facet_scales

Axis scale argument passed to facet_wrap / facet_grid: "free" (default), "fixed", "free_x", or "free_y".

x_limits

Numeric vector of length 2 for x-axis limits, or NULL for automatic limits. Example: c(0, 1) for proportions.

x_lab

X-axis label string. NULL auto-derives from plot_cols: a single column name is title-cased; multiple columns produce "Value".

y_lab

Y-axis label string. NULL auto-derives from group_by.

title

Plot title string.

subtitle

Plot subtitle string, or NULL for none.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Multi-column mode (plot_cols): when more than one column is supplied, the data are pivoted to long format and each column becomes a row of panels.

See also

nhood_diversity, nhood_shm, nhood_cdr3_convergence, plot_nhood_scatter

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Single-metric plot
plot_nhood_beeswarm(
  nhood_data      = nhood_data,
  plot_cols       = "shannon_diversity",
  group_by        = "anat",
  reliability_col = "diversity_reliable",
  subtitle        = paste0("Reliable estimates (>=", attr(nhood_data, "min_bcr_tcr"), " BCR/TCR)")
)

# Multi-column plot
plot_nhood_beeswarm(
  nhood_data = ccall_df,
  plot_cols  = c("IgA", "IgG", "IgM"),
  group_by   = "anat",
  x_limits   = c(0, 1),
  x_lab      = "Proportion of Cells"
)

# Point size mapped to a column, with a custom size range
plot_nhood_beeswarm(
  nhood_data = nhood_data,
  plot_cols  = "shannon_diversity",
  group_by   = "anat",
  size_by    = "nhood_size",
  size       = c(1, 6)
)
} # }
